stages.name: Requested
stages.instructions: Triage. Messaging work (positioning, announcement briefs, sequences) is moved to `messaging`; community work (issue/discussion digests, feedback triage, reply drafts) is moved to `community`. A card goes to ONE lane. Nothing advances out of this stage on its own.

stages.name: Messaging brief
stages.instructions: Produce a DRAFT only: one audience per brief, plain words, every claim linked to verified shipped work (merged PR, release, changelog). Attach the brief as a reference. Do not post, schedule, DM, promise dates, or contact anyone outside this board. Hand drafting of final copy to Writer Quill and visuals to Artistic Lyra as recommendations, not as queued work.

stages.name: Cleared to publish
stages.instructions: Approved by a person. Publishing is done by a person, by hand; then move the card to `done`. Nothing advances out of this stage on its own, so an approved brief never flows into the community lane.

stages.name: Community triage
stages.instructions: Produce DRAFTS only: count recurring questions before concluding, link every item to its public source, and write reply drafts that make no promises or dates. Recommend documentation/product gaps. Attach the digest and drafts as references. Never post a reply, comment, react, label, or DM anyone.

stages.name: Cleared to reply
stages.instructions: Approved by a person. Replies are posted by a person, by hand; then move the card to `done`. Nothing advances out of this stage on its own.

metadata.audience: Workspace administrators and owners registering a coordinator agent
metadata.singleMessage: Registration is a human-controlled setup that gives the coordinator only the access needed to work a dispatched card.
metadata.brief: DRAFT — Audience: Workspace administrators and owners registering a coordinator agent; single message: registration is a human-controlled setup that gives the coordinator only the access it needs to work a dispatched card. The published operator guide documents the administrator actions—define the capability, create and link the agent, mint two tokens, add it to a station, and queue a first card—and says agent credentials are refused for every one of them. After dispatch, the coordinator’s run-only credential can drive the card it already holds but cannot claim another; follow the guide to complete the administrator setup and verify the first matching card is claimed in the board log.

references.title: DRAFT community triage — SuperPipeline issue #117
references.subtitle: One-source report: cost accounting cannot represent unpriced usage without misleading partial totals

metadata.category: Product/engineering gap — usage-cost data model and reporting accuracy
metadata.summary: Issue #117 reports that ACP can carry cost and Claude Code has emitted USD costs, but agentpod currently drops that field. SuperPipeline stores cost_usd as non-null with a zero default, so genuinely free and unknown/unpriced runs are indistinguishable; forwarding only known costs could make mixed-harness totals look complete when they are partial. The requested direction is explicit unpriced state through storage, rollups, budget behavior, and UI disclosure.
metadata.replyDraft: Thanks, @fixture-user — the distinction between $0 and unknown/unpriced is clear, and the mixed-harness example explains why forwarding only the reported Claude Code amount could overstate the completeness of a board total. We’ve captured this as a product/engineering gap spanning usage storage, rollups/budget semantics, agentpod forwarding, and UI disclosure. To evaluate the edge cases, could you clarify the expected treatment when one run contains both priced and unpriced usage updates, and how the budget gate should behave when any amount remains unpriced? Source: https://github.com/SuperJackfruitLabs/superpipeline/issues/117
metadata.missingEvidence: Only one issue was reviewed, with no comments, so this is one report rather than a recurring theme. The issue does not establish expected behavior for mixed priced/unpriced events within one run; budget-gate behavior under unknown cost; non-USD cost handling/conversion; or reproducible code/version references and tests for the cited coalescer, schema, rollups, and UI behavior.
metadata.recommendation: Treat as a product/engineering data-model gap, not a documentation-only fix. Define priced/unpriced semantics and budget behavior first; then document how partial totals are represented. No outward reply or GitHub mutation was made.
